rationale: The left leg is verbatim identical to the archived "Capex Cash-Coverage Maturity Strain" (capx/at − che/at, IND_RANK'd) and the conditioner merely appends NEG(oancf/at) to the same dlc/lt term, making this a cosmetic conditioner extension of an already strongly-tested signal rather than a new mechanism.

The lagged-capex leg replicates "Failed Prior Capex Payoff" exactly and the substituted conditioner legs (NEG(DELTA(oancf/at)), dlc/lt) are both already used elsewhere in the archive, so this is a recombination of tested components with no new economic content beyond swapping sales-productivity decay for cash-flow decay.

This is the only proposal with a genuinely distinct left leg — a five-year trend in noncash, noninventory current assets scaled by sales rather than assets — which extends the working-capital channel toward receivables stretch in a way not directly covered by the archived one-year DELTA version, though it shares conceptual overlap with the well-known receivables/net-operating-asset accrual anomaly and reuses a heavily-recycled distress conditioner.

This is "Inventory Credit Squeeze Trend" with a single conditioner leg swapped from NEG(che/at) to NEG(re/at); the left leg and the DELTA(dlc/lt) term are unchanged, so it is a cosmetic variant of one of the archive's strongest existing results and will mostly re-estimate the same portfolio.

Direct rediscovery of the archived "Overstaffed Rollover Burden" with the only change being dlc/lt → lct/act in the conditioner — two highly correlated short-term-pressure proxies — leaving the hypothesis and expected mechanism verbatim identical.

The gdwl/sale leg is identical to "Goodwill Revenue-Support Failure" and the goodwill × leverage/weak-profitability interaction is additionally covered by "Goodwill Impairment Pressure," so this is a third permutation of the same conditioner space rather than a new channel.
